Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of EMERGENCY RESCUE SERVICES Suggested Vocabulary red cross, ambulance, emergency,  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Which words have the same spelling but different meanings? 2. Why is it important to pronounce words accurately?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Pronounce words containing the sound /ʊə/. Learners with speech difficulties could be allowed extra time to make presentations  Pronounce words with same spelling but different meanings,  Work with peers in purposive groups to distinguish verbs, nouns and adjectives on the basis of stress, for example, extract/extract, perfect /perfect,  Work with peers to make a recording of the poetry recitation. a song on emergency rescue services and lay emphasis on content words Learners with manipulation difficulties could 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: The learner’s ability to speak effectively is improved as they pronounce words containing the target sound.

Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to interact with technology as they make recordings of songs and poetry recitations.

Values:
Unity The learner strives to achieve a common goal while working with peers to distinguish verbs, nouns and adjectives on the

basis of stress.
